exchanges: Hi. Long day. We moved into the Hamilton house on Saturday and I'm still finding things in the wrong boxes.
That sounds exhausting. Moving week always has a box that holds the one thing you need.
the kettle was in a box labelled BATHROOM. i dont know who packed that. me. i packed that
At least it turned up. Tea makes unpacking a little more bearable.
kwame starts grade 6 tomorrow, hes nervous but wont admit it
That's very grade 6 of him. A new school at that age is a lot.
we went to see the school last week and he got into dundurn which is like a 5 min walk which is the main reason i picked this street honestly
A five minute walk is a huge win for mornings.
the cats are adjusting... mango is fine, tofu hid in the dryer for two days
Sounds like a classic anxious cat. The dryer is a cozy, dark hiding spot.
i checked the dryer before running it dont worry lol
Good habit to keep, especially with a hider.
ok so kwame's first day was fine. he made a friend named jun who also likes minecraft
Minecraft is the universal grade 6 friendship language.
so the other thing going on. his old teacher in ottawa thought he might have adhd and recommended an assessment, so ive been trying to get one here
That can take some navigating in a new city. A pediatrician referral is usually the first step.
yes we got in with a pediatrician, dr abernathy, she was great with him, really patient. she's referring us to a psychologist for the full assessment
That's a good start. Having a doctor who connects with him will help through the process.
the wait for the psychologist is four months. ugh
Four months is frustrating but sadly pretty common. You could ask the school about interim supports.
my neighbour giulia came by with treats. she runs a bakery on locke street. the cannoli were unreal
Fresh treats on your doorstep is a great welcome to the neighbourhood.
she has a son kwame's age, so thats good
Built-in neighbourhood friend, even better.
my aunt wanjiru called from mississauga, she wants to visit but her diabetes has been all over the place so she's not sure she can drive
Hopefully it settles soon. Maybe a train would be easier for her.
yeah the go train is an option. she'd probably bring my mom's aunt njeri too, who is 89 and slowly losing her sight from glaucoma but refuses to stop travelling
She sounds like a force. Travelling with company makes sense at that age.
theyre both tough as nails
Sounds like it runs in the family.
i signed up for a yoga class at the community centre. first one tonight
That's a nice thing to do for yourself in the middle of everything.
the teacher is ravi, very gentle, very good at making beginners feel ok
That's the most important thing in a beginner class.
Correction on Giulia, by the way: it's not a bakery, it's a gelato shop. I assumed because of the cannoli, but she sells those as a side thing.
Ah, that's even better for summer. Kwame will probably become a regular.
he already asked if we can go every day lol. no
A firm no is fair. Maybe a Friday treat instead.
his old school in ottawa was westdale, and his new teacher already emailed asking for his records
Good that she's on top of it. That'll help with the assessment too.
emeka called, wants kwame for thanksgiving. hes flying back from his routes in europe anyway, being a pilot hes never home
Thanksgiving with his dad could be nice for Kwame after a big change.
yoga was good tonight. after class ravi was chatting and it turns out he used to be a dentist for 15 years before he quit to teach
That's a big career switch. He must really love it.
he said he burned out and yoga saved him. i get it
Sounds like you're finding some of that calm yourself.
maybe. my shoulders are less tight anyway
That's a good sign after just a couple of classes.

questions.message: whats going on with my great aunts health again
what school is kwame going to now
giulias the one with the bakery right
what does my aunt wanjiru do for work
might try the morning class too if i can drag myself out of bed
